fields.name: Infernal Contract (HB)
fields.components: V, M (100gp worth of magical inks, which the spell consumes)
fields.classes: School: Enchantment, Bard, Cleric, Warlock, Wizard, Warlock (Fiend)
fields.text:
Monsters: Hags, Devils, Archmages, Liches, Warlocks of the Fiend (at will, as ritual)

Invoking the laws of the Pact Primeval, you bind willing creatures into a contract which ensures everyone involved upholds their end of the bargain.
	In preparation for you casting the spell, each entity to be involved with and bound by the contract must willingly provide a vial of its own blood, which is then mixed with ink. The magical ink used to draft this contract cannot be made invisible, glows red, and is warm to the touch. Additionally, any text written with this ink can be understood by entities whose blood has been used in the ink's creation, regardless of the language or handwriting style used.
	The spell can only be cast if all entities whose blood is mixed with the ink have signed it with their true names. Whenever a clause is added or removed, any existing signature disappears. If a creature has less than 8 Intelligence, Wisdom and/or Charisma at the moment the spell is cast, if it has been coerced by force, threats or magic into signing, or if it signs with anything other than its true name, the magic does not take hold, and the spell's components are wasted.
	The contract bursts in flames after it is signed by all involved parties. From the moment the contract is in effect to the moment it is terminated, all involved parties can magically summon or dismiss a copy of the contract into existence as an action. Unless specified otherwise, the contract is terminated when one of the parties dies.
	The contract must contain at least the following two elements: commitments and exit clauses.

Commitments:
Each party involved makes one or more promises to the other parties. If one of the commitments is not met, then the contract is terminated, and the exit clause for the party who failed to deliver on their promise is invoked.
	This magical contract allows you to do transactions that could not be performed without magic. However, the contract cannot allow you to give something you do not possess. Here are examples of possible commitments:

	• Arcane Power. You give the recipient some of the spells you know, and some of your spell slots. The recipient can cast those spells, using those spell slots. They use their own spellcasting ability modifier, using the same Ability Score you would have used to cast those spells. These spells and spell slots are not available to you anymore, until the contract is terminated. This is often what is offered to Warlocks.

	• Memory. The recipient is given your memory of an event. The contract may let you keep a copy of these memories, or they are lost to you until the contract is terminated. This is often used in courts, to ensure the veracity of a testimony.

	• A sense. You can decide to either give, or share a sense with another party. If you give your sense of sight to a blind person, they will regain their vision, but you will lose yours. You could decide to share a sense instead. If you do, the blind person will not regain their vision-instead, they will see everything that you see, from your point of view, until the contract is terminated.

	• A favor. You can specify a task to be completed before a certain date. Alternatively, you can specify a number of favors to be reclaimed later.

	• Your eternal soul. If an entity possesses your soul, they can summon your soul within 30 feet of them as an action, or dismiss your soul back to where it was before you were summoned in the same way. They can read your thoughts, and have access to all of your memories. You are unable to disobey any verbal or telepathic command they give you, and they know if you tell them a lie. Finally, while your soul is forfeit, you cannot sign any additional infernal contract.

Unless specified otherwise within the contract, when the contract is terminated for any reason, the contract magically returns any item, experience, memory, sense, favor, or soul that had been given to their original owners.
	If a commitment can be interpreted in different ways, the party who makes the commitment decides which interpretation is correct when they make it.

Exit Clauses:
You must describe what happens to each party should they fail to deliver on their commitments within the agreed upon timeframe. Again, the contract can enforce things through the use of magic that would otherwise be impossible. Here are examples of common exit clauses:

	• Curse. The faulty party receives a curse, as per the bestow curse spell, as if it had been cast as a 9th level spell. They fail the saving throw automatically.

	• Recall. The faulty party is teleported to the location where the contract was signed.

	• Imprisonment. The faulty party is imprisoned, as per the imprisonment spell, for a duration to be specified. They fail the saving throw automatically.

	• Compensation. The faulty party makes a new commitment as a penalty. For example, the party could have their ability to speak taken away as punishment.

	• Punishment. The faulty party suffers one of the effects of the symbol spell. They fail the saving throw automatically.

A wish spell can be used to terminate the contract without being subjected to its exit clauses.
	If an exit clause can be interpreted in different ways, the parties who did not fail their commitments decide which interpretation is correct when the exit clause is invoked.
	Long ago, the Fey collectively signed an infernal contract which made it so their word became magically binding. Because of this, any promise or agreement made orally to or by a fey creature instantly results in the casting of this spell, with clauses determined automatically.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 45 (Indie)

fields.name: Jinx (HB)
fields.time: 1 reaction, which you take when a creature within range rolls with advantage
fields.classes: School: Enchantment, Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
When a creature within 30 feet that you can see makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw with advantage, you can use your reaction to remove advantage from the attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 46 (Indie)

fields.name: Mark of the Companion (HB)
fields.classes: School: Transmutation, Touch Spells, Cleric, Druid, Ranger
fields.text:
You can use this magic as a means of transporting bonded creature companions, blending in with busy city streets, or hiding them away during stealthy endeavors.
	As an action, you can touch a willing creature with a CR up to 1/3 of your level and absorb their essence into your body. For as long as you concentrate up to 8 hours (or until you use an action to end the effect early) the companion appears on your body as a mark that relates to them. This can be a claw scar, an eagle tattoo, or even a birthmark in the shape of an otter. You can choose a new appearance every time you cast this spell. While absorbed this way, the companion sees what you see and can communicate telepathically with you as if they were walking right alongside you.
	When the spell ends, the creature appears in the nearest unoccupied space of your choice.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 46 (Indie)

fields.name: Misadventure (HB)
fields.classes: School: Abjuration, Bard, Cleric, Ranger, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
You extrude an aura of ill luck. You have the option to make any attack roll, ability check, or saving throw during this spell's duration with disadvantage. Each time you do, creatures you designate within 30 feet of you also have disadvantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw that they make within the next 1 minute.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 46 (Indie)

fields.name: Misfortune (HB)
fields.text:
Creatures (including yourself) within 30 feet that you can see make ability checks, attack rolls, or saving throws at disadvantage.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 47 (Indie)

fields.name: Partial Absorption (HB)
fields.time: 1 reaction, which you take when you
fields.classes: School: Abjuration, Artificer, Bard, Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Ranger
fields.text:
When you or a creature within 30 feet of you takes damage from a spell or magical effect, you can use your reaction to grant yourself or another creature within 30 feet of you resistance to damage from spells and other magical effects for that instance of damage.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 47 (Indie)

fields.name: Possession (HB)
fields.text:
You can attempt to possess a creature by transforming into a pure spiritual force to take control of it. One humanoid that you can see within 5 feet of you must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be possessed by you; you then disappear, and the target is incapacitated and loses control of its body. You now control the body but don't deprive the target of awareness. You can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that turn undead, and you retain your alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and class abilities and features. You otherwise use the possessed target's statistics, but don't gain access to the target's knowledge, features, or proficiencies. The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 hit points, you end it as a bonus action, or you are turned or forced out by an effect such as dispel evil and good. When the possession ends, you reappear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the body in your true form. The target is immune to this spell for 24 hours after succeeding on the saving throw or after the spell ends.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 47 (Indie)

fields.name: Shared Destiny (HB)
fields.classes: School: Enchantment, Bard, Cleric, Paladin, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
You weave a thread that binds a creature's life to your own, shielding you and channeling harm to the creature. You target one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. A crackling cord of variegated energy tethers you to the target. Whenever you take damage, the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you take half the damage (rounded down), and the target takes the remaining damage.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 48 (Indie)

fields.name: Speak with Monsters (HB)
fields.classes: School: Divination, Artificer, Bard, Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Ranger, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
This spell allows you to communicate with a monster (designated by you when you cast the spell) as if you both shared a language.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 48 (Indie)

fields.name: Spell Eater (HB)
fields.time: 1 reaction, which you take when you see a creature within 90 feet of you casting a spell
fields.classes: School: Abjuration, Bard, Cleric, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
You can use your reaction to absorb a spell that you and only you are the target of. The absorbed spell's effect is canceled, and you either regain a number of temporary hit points equal to five times the level of the spell or you end one condition affecting you.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 48 (Indie)

fields.name: Terror Strike (HB)
fields.classes: School: Enchantment, Artificer, Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
As a part of this spell, make a melee attack with a weapon available to you. When you roll your attack roll, also roll 5d8; the total is how many hit points of creatures this spell can affect. All the creatures of your choice within 90 feet of you are affected in ascending order of their current hit points. Starting with the creature that has the lowest current hit points, each creature affected by this spell becomes frightened of you until either the spell ends or when they succeed on a wisdom saving throw against this spell. A creature can attempt this saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effects on themselves on a success. Subtract each creature's hit points from the total before moving on to the creature with the next lowest hit points. A creature's hit points must be equal to or less than the remaining total for that creature to be affected.

At Higher Levels: If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, roll an extra 2d8 for each spell slot above 1st.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 48 (Indie)

fields.name: Wall of Mud (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a ball of clay)
fields.text:
You create a wall of clinging clay. You choose to make the wall up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick, or a circle that has a 20-foot diameter and is up to 20 feet high and 5 feet thick. The wall blocks line of sight. The terrain 10 feet around each section of the wall becomes thick with sticky clay, creating difficult terrain. Moving through an affected square consumes 3 feet of movement per 1 foot moved. Each 5-foot-square wall section has AC 10 and 10 hit points. Reducing a section to 0 hit points destroys that section and removes the difficult terrain in a 5-foot-radius around it.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 48 (Indie)

fields.name: Weave Access (HB)
fields.classes: School: Enchantment, Artificer, Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
You draw the Weave to yourself to connect to the very essence of magic. Whenever you make an Arcana check, a concentration check, or an ability check using your spellcasting ability, you can roll a d6 and add the number rolled to the check.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can add +1 to the check or roll for each slot above 2nd level.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 49 (Indie)

fields.name: Well of Levitation (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a feather and tuning fork)
fields.text:
Select a 20-foot square within range. Each creature in the chosen area must make a Constitution saving throw or rise vertically, up to 20 feet, and remain suspended there for the duration. The spell can levitate targets that weigh up to 1000 pounds.
	The target can move only by pushing or pulling against a fixed object or surface within reach (such as a wall or a ceiling), which allows it to move as if it were climbing. As a bonus action, you can choose to lower or raise each creature in the area by 20 feet and up to 60 feet into the air. If you are the target, you can move up or down as part of your move. Otherwise, you can use your bonus action to move the target, which must remain within the spell's range.
	When the spell ends, the target floats gently to the ground if it is still aloft.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 49 (Indie)

fields.name: Burst Maneuver: Deafening Blast
fields.text:
A creature within 5 feet of you when you fired the shot must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be deafened for 1 minute. This creature doesn't need to be the target of the attack that caused the gunpowder burst.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 84 (Indie)

fields.name: Burst Maneuver: Hobble
fields.text:
Your weapon's burst damaged the target's leg, wing, or other ambulatory limb. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or its speed is reduced by 10 feet until it receives magical healing or finishes a short or long rest. This effect is cumulative, but it can't reduce a target's speed to less than 5 feet.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 84 (Indie)

fields.name: Burst Maneuver: Penetrating Shot
fields.text:
If your target is Large or smaller, the burst causes the shot to go through your target. If another creature is within 10 feet of the target, and a direct line can be drawn from the creature to you with the original target in between, then the new creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take damage as if hit by a normal attack from the weapon. This damage can't burst.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 84 (Indie)

fields.name: Burst Maneuver: Powerful Shot
fields.text:
The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone by the burst.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 84 (Indie)

fields.name: Burst Maneuver: Pummel
fields.text:
The power of the burst empowers you to strike a nearby creature. You can make one melee weapon attack with a melee weapon you are wielding against a creature within your melee weapon's range.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 84 (Indie)

fields.name: Burst Maneuver: Smoke Cloud
fields.text:
The shot produces a large amount of smoke, heavily obscuring your space until the start of your next turn.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 84 (Indie)

fields.name: Burst Maneuver: Soft Spot
fields.text:
Your weapon's burst causes the target an extreme amount of pain. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be incapacitated until the start of your next turn.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 84 (Indie)

fields.name: Burst Maneuver: Sudden Advance
fields.text:
The burst energizes you, causing you to leap into action. You can immediately move up to half your speed. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 84 (Indie)

fields.name: Burst Maneuver: Unsteadying Shot
fields.text:
The burst destabilized the target. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have disadvantage on all attacks until the start of your next turn.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 84 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Chaotic Aegis (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 5th level, Wyrdweaver patron

The pact with your patron offers protection from the powers of entropy. When you or a creature targeting you with an effect must roll a die or dice and consult a table to determine the outcome of the effect, such as with the confusion spell, you can use your reaction to force a reroll of the die or dice. You must use the new result. You must finish a short or long rest before you can use this invocation again.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 134 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Chaotic Luck (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 3rd level, Wyrdweaver patron

The tumbling dice of fate sometimes fall in your favor. When you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to force the attacker to reroll the damage dice. You must accept the new damage roll. You must finish a short or long rest before you can use this invocation again.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

name: Eldritch Invocation: Convulsions of the World (HB)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Convulsions of the World (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 3rd level

Your mind reaches deep into the ground and an elder voice answers. You can use an action to cause a localized tremor to shake the ground around you. Each creature other than yourself within 20 feet of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone. You can choose a number of creatures equal to half your proficiency bonus to automatically succeed on this saving throw. You must finish a long rest before you can use this invocation again.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Doom Hound (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 7th level, Pact of the Chain feature, Hunter in Darkness patron

As a bonus action, your familiar transforms into a more powerful creature for 1 minute. At 7th level and higher, it transforms into a dire wolf. At 12th level and higher, it transforms into a winter wolf. At 18th level and higher, it transforms into a hound of the night (see Tome of Beasts). You must finish a short or long rest before you can use this invocation on your familiar again.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Earthblood Geyser (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 15th level

Tapping the living mind of the world, you call forth retribution from the ground. You can cast magma spray (see the Magic and Spells chapter) at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

name: Eldritch Invocation: Echo of the First Words (HB)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Echo of the First Words (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 9th level, Primordial patron

The echo of the first magical utterance reverberates across time, confounding those who hear it. You can cast babble once using a warlock spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Entangling Blast (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 5th level, eldritch blast cantrip, Old Wood patron

When you hit a creature with eldritch blast, the creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by roots, vines, and other vegetation until the end of its next turn. The DC for this saving throw and to escape this grapple is your spell save DC.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Extinguishing Blast (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: eldritch blast cantrip, Hunter in Darkness patron

When you hit a creature with eldritch blast, you reduce the light surrounding it until the end of your next turn. If the creature is in bright light, the area within 10 feet of it becomes dim light. If the creature is in dim light, the area within 10 feet of it becomes darkness.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Forest-Trained (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: eldritch blast cantrip, Hunter in Darkness patron

You gain proficiency in the Nature and Survival skills.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Green Thumb (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 5th level, Old Wood patron

You can cast plant growth once using a warlock spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Improved Companion (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 12th level, Patron Companion feature

When your patron sends you a beast as part of your Patron Companion feature, you can choose a beast that relates to your patron (as shown in the beast type column in the Animal Lords table) that has a challenge rating of 3 or lower.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

name: Eldritch Invocation: Knowledge of the Wood (HB)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Knowledge of the Wood (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 15th level, Old Wood patron

When you are within 5 feet of a body of water in a forest, you can cast scrying on any creature in that forest at will, without expending a warlock spell slot or material components. You must remain within 5 feet of the body of water for the duration or the spell ends.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Lurker in Gloom (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 7th level, Hunter in Darkness patron

As a reaction when you take damage while in dim light or darkness, you wrap shadows around yourself and have resistance to that instance of damage. Once you use this invocation, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Nature's Armor (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: Old Wood patron

You can use your action to sprout hard thorns across your skin for 1 hour. Your Armor Class becomes 12 + your Dexterity modifier, and, when a creature hits you with a melee weapon attack while within 5 feet of you, it takes piercing damage equal to half your warlock level. You must finish a short or long rest before you can use this invocation again.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 136 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Patient Hunter (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: Pact of the Tome feature, Hunter in Darkness patron

When you identify a creature's tracks using your tome, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) and Wisdom (Survival) checks to find and track the creature for the next 24 hours.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 136 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Primal Link (HB)
fields.text:
You can cast animal friendship at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 136 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Shadow Arrow (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 12th level, Pact of the Blade feature, Hunter in Darkness patron

When you hit a creature with an arrow shot from your pact weapon, you can fire a second, shadow arrow at the creature as a bonus action. If it hits, the shadow arrow deals necrotic damage equal to the damage dealt by the first arrow.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 136 (Indie)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Silent Stalker (HB)
fields.text:
You gain proficiency in the Stealth and Survival skills.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 136 (Indie)

name: Eldritch Invocation: Speaker for the Trees (HB)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Speaker for the Trees (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 9th level, Old Wood patron

You can cast speak with plants at will without expending a spell slot.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 136 (Indie)

name: Eldritch Invocation: Touch of the Forest (HB)

fields.name: Eldritch Invocation: Touch of the Forest (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 9th level, Old Wood patron

You can cast awaken once using a warlock spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 136 (Indie)

fields.name: Abrupt Hug (HB)
fields.time: 1 reaction, which you take when you or a creature within 30 feet of you takes an Attack action
fields.text:
You or the creature taking the Attack action can immediately make an unarmed strike. In addition to dealing damage with the unarmed strike, the target can grapple the creature it hit with the unarmed strike.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 273 (Indie)

fields.name: Adjust Position (HB)
fields.text:
You adjust the location of an ally to a better tactical position. You move one willing creature within range 5 feet. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. The creature moves bodily through the intervening space (as opposed to teleporting), so there can be no physical obstacle (such as a wall or a door) in the path.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can target an additional willing creature for each slot level above 1st.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 273 (Indie)

fields.name: Ambush (HB)
fields.components: S, M (a raven's feather or a bit of panther fur)
fields.text:
The forest floor swirls and shifts around you to welcome you into its embrace. While in a forest, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to Hide. While hidden in a forest, you have advantage on your next Initiative check. The spell ends if you attack or cast a spell.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can affect one additional creature for each slot level above 1st. The spell ends if you or any target of this spell attacks or casts a spell.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 273 (Indie)

fields.name: Ambush Chute (HB)
fields.text:
You touch a wooden, plaster, or stone surface and create a passage with two trapdoors. The first trapdoor appears where you touch the surface, and the other appears at a point you can see up to 30 feet away. The two trapdoors can be wooden with a metal ring handle, or they can match the surrounding surfaces, each with a small notch for opening the door. The two trapdoors are connected by an extradimensional passage that is up to 5 feet wide, up to 5 feet tall, and up to 30 feet long. The trapdoors don't need to be on the same surface, allowing the passage to connect two separated locations, such as the two sides of a chasm or river. The passage is always straight and level for creatures inside it, and the creatures exit the tunnel in such a way that allows them to maintain the same orientation as when they entered the passage. No more than five creatures can transit the passage at the same time.
	When the spell ends and the trapdoors disappear, any creatures or objects still in the passage created by the spell are safely ejected to an unoccupied space nearest the end of the passage closest to them.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the length of the passage and the distance you can place the second trapdoor increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 3rd.

Source:	Tome of Heroes p. 273 (Indie)
